fair_value.method: Forward P/E on the earnings the market will price in Sept 2027: FY2028 EPS of about $10.50 (consensus FY2027 $9.58 from 40 analysts, plus ~9-10% growth from mid-single-digit revenue growth and ~2.5%/yr net buyback shrink, less a memory-cost gross margin headwind) x 31.5x (a premium to Apple's ~28-30x 5-year forward average for AI/foldable optionality and services mix, but below today's ~35x given services decelerating toward ~9.5% and margin pressure) = ~$330.

bear.story: Memory inflation (the '100-year flood') persists through FY2027, gross margin stuck near 46-47%, supply constraints on advanced nodes cap iPhone units, iPhone Duo demand disappoints at $1,999+, services slows below 9%; FY2027 EPS ~ $9.0-9.3 and the multiple de-rates to ~26x on FY2028 ~$9.7.

base.story: iPhone 18 cycle and Duo roughly meet expectations, price increases offset most memory costs, gross margin recovers to ~47.5-48%, services grows ~9-10%, buybacks ~$90-100B/yr; FY2028 EPS ~ $10.6 on a modestly compressed ~32.5x.

bull.story: Siri AI (iOS 27) drives a genuine multi-year upgrade supercycle, Duo lifts ASPs, supply constraints ease and memory prices roll over in 2027; FY2028 EPS ~ $11.5+ and the market holds a ~37x multiple as Apple is re-rated as an AI distribution winner.

thesis_break_reason: About 30% below the current $341 and below the 52-week low ($243.42). At $240 Apple would trade at ~25x consensus FY2027 EPS, a level that only makes sense if earnings power itself is impaired: e.g. a sustained gross margin reset from memory costs, a failed iPhone 18/Duo cycle, loss of the ~$20B Google payment or a forced App Store economics change, or a China/tariff shock. Ordinary 25% vol would take the stock there less than ~10% of the time.

catalysts.event: iPhone Duo pre-orders open (ships 2026-10-23); first read on foldable demand at ~$1,999
Fiscal Q4 2026 earnings, first under CEO John Ternus; guide for December quarter, memory cost and gross margin outlook
Fiscal Q1 2027 (holiday quarter) earnings: iPhone 18/Duo sell-through, supply constraints
Fiscal Q2 2027 earnings plus annual capital return update (buyback authorization, dividend)
WWDC 2027: next-gen Siri/Apple Intelligence roadmap, EU/China AI rollout status
Fiscal Q3 2027 earnings; services growth trajectory and FY2028 margin setup
iPhone 19 launch event (reports say all-glass model cancelled per Jefferies)
DOJ v. Apple antitrust case, Google search remedy appeals, memory (DRAM/NAND) contract pricing, tariffs

key_uncertainties: Duration and size of memory cost inflation and Apple's ability to pass it through (guided Q4 GM 47-48% vs 50.1% in Q3, which had ~2pts of tariff refunds)
Whether the stock holds a ~35x forward multiple with EPS growth of ~9% and services decelerating toward ~9.5%
Real demand for iPhone Duo and whether Siri AI (iOS 27) drives an upgrade cycle; AI features delayed in EU and China
Advanced-node supply constraints limiting iPhone/Mac/iPad shipments
Regulatory: Google default-search payments (~$20B/yr) under appeal scrutiny; DOJ monopolization case; App Store fee rules
New CEO transition (Ternus from 2026-09-01) and broader AI-sector valuation sentiment
reasoning: Apple closed at $341.07, near an all-time high (~$345) after a +35% year, driven by strong June-quarter results (revenue $109.4B +16%, iPhone +22%, EPS $2.02 +29% incl. $0.11 tariff refunds), the iPhone 18 cycle, the $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable (ships Oct 23) and a well-received Siri AI relaunch. Against that: Q4 guidance of only +9-11% revenue with GM falling to 47-48% on memory costs Cook called a '100-year flood', services decelerating (12% in Q3, MS expects ~9.5% in Q4), multiple downgrades (Jefferies Underperform ~$264, Phillip Capital) and a consensus mean target (~$328, median $340) at or below the price. Valuation: consensus FY2027 EPS $9.58 (range $8.69-10.67), so the stock is ~35.6x FY2027; by Sept 2027 investors will price FY2028 (~$10.5). At a still-premium 31.5x that gives ~$330 fair value, i.e. the stock is fully valued and returns must come from EPS growth (~9%) roughly offset by modest multiple compression, plus 0.3% dividend. So I centered the distribution with a median of ~$341 (flat), expected value ~$342 from scenarios (bear $250 25% / base $345 50% / bull $430 25%). For dispersion I used a lognormal with sigma ~27% (realized vol 25%, bumped for event risk around memory margins, new CEO, and a high starting multiple that makes de-rating risk asymmetric) and fattened both tails slightly: P(>=$239) 0.89, P(>=$409) 0.24, P(>=$512) 0.055. Deep tails (<$171 or >$597) require a crash in a $5T megacap or a >75% rally and are assigned 1-2.5%. I did not consult option prices or implied vol.
